speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To begin my assessment, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and did they start after a specific injury or event?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy with radiculopathy.

Based on your chronic burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness over three months, I suspect compression of the spinal cord and nerve roots in your neck. Given your age and history of motor vehicle accident, we need to confirm the extent of this compression. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI. REQUEST TEST: Electrodiagnostic_studies.
